newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Fighting around Sierra Leone military headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Fighting around Sierra Leone military headquarters.

text.p: Fighting broke out around the beachfront military headquarters in Sierra Leone's capital on Monday after Nigerian ships began a bombardment against coup leaders at daybreak, witnesses said.

Soldiers who toppled civilian President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah on May 25 are based in the complex. Negotiations there on Sunday night between coup leaders and British and Nigerian diplomats failed to reach an agreement.
A Reuters reporter saw the bodies of a couple and their grandson in the Aberdeen district who were killed when a shell from the Nigerian ships hit their house.

Rebels allied to the coup leaders and Sierra Leonean soldiers exchanged fire with Nigerian troops protecting a hotel near the military headquarters in which about 1,000 West African foreigners are holed up. The foreigners took refuge in the hotel basement. First and second floor windows were shattered by incoming fire.
Four Nigerian soldiers were brought into the hotel with light gunshot wounds.
A spokesman for the coup leaders speaking on state radio urged people to come out and protest against the Nigerian intervention.
